original_question: For the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a smoothly bounded domain Omega subset of R^N with N >= 3, u = 0 on partial Omega, and 2* = 2N/(N-2), is there a more direct proof, ideally a variational one, of the three-dimensional result on the unit ball B(0,1) stating that for every lambda > 0 there exist infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the paper's first concluding open question: whether the recent three-dimensional unit-ball resolution of Brezis's first open problem admits a substantially more direct proof, preferably a variational one. The nearby historical discussion in the paper singles out the Sun-Wei-Yang result that, on the unit ball in dimension 3, one has infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions for every λ>0. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core PDE right, includes the Dirichlet boundary condition, identifies the special three-dimensional unit-ball setting B(0,1)⊂R^3, and focuses on the specific stronger conclusion highlighted near the paper's discussion of [57]: for every λ>0 there are infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions. It also matches the paper's meta-question about a more direct proof, ideally variational. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should be specialized all the way to N=3 and Ω=B_1:=B(0,1), so that 2*=6 and the equation becomes -Δu=λu+|u|^4u in B_1 with u=0 on ∂B_1, rather than starting from the general N-dimensional formulation. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046?utm_source=openai))

The natural function class should be stated explicitly: one seeks nontrivial weak solutions u∈H_0^1(B_1), which are then smooth by elliptic regularity. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046?utm_source=openai))

The question should identify the result as the recent Sun-Wei-Yang resolution referred to in the paper, rather than as an unnamed 'three-dimensional result'. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046?utm_source=openai))

It is helpful to make explicit that 'non-radial' means not invariant under rotations about the center of B_1, and that 'sign-changing' means both positive and negative parts are nontrivial. This is implicit in the draft but not stated. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06904?utm_source=openai))

For paper-faithfulness, the question should note the relation to Brezis's original open problem: the original problem asked only for existence of a nontrivial solution for 0<λ≤λ_1(B_1)/4=π^2/4, whereas the cited recent theorem is stronger, giving infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions for every λ>0. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/40170))

Because the paper's open-question list appears to ask for a direct/variational proof of this specific 3D phenomenon, the refined question should avoid broadening to general smoothly bounded domains or to dimensions other than 3. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/tw/review/on-brezis-nirenberg-problems-open-questions-and-new-results-in-dimension-six))
refined_question:
For the three-dimensional Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem on the unit ball B_1:=B(0,1)⊂R^3,
-Δu=λu+|u|^4u in B_1,
 u∈H_0^1(B_1),
can one give a substantially more direct proof—preferably a purely variational proof—that for every λ>0 there exist infinitely many solutions u that are sign-changing (u^+≢0 and u^-≢0) and non-radial with respect to the center of B_1, thereby in particular recovering the recent full resolution of Brezis's first open problem in this setting?
justification: This rewrite stays as narrow as the paper's intent: it does not generalize beyond the 3D unit ball, and it keeps the exact stronger conclusion emphasized in the paper's historical discussion of [57], namely infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions for every λ>0. I only made explicit the hidden data that are needed to make the question mathematically autonomous: B_1⊂R^3, exponent 6, the solution space H_0^1(B_1), and the meaning of 'sign-changing' and 'non-radial'. I also recorded the connection with Brezis's original Open Problem 1.1 (the range 0<λ≤π^2/4 on B_1), because that is the conceptual reason this question matters, while keeping the actual target fixed at the stronger theorem the paper discusses. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046?utm_source=openai))
